after.title: Tailgate Support Cables Can Corrode and Fracture (Recall 04V129)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 04V129 covers certain 2002-2004 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles. The galvanized-steel cables that hold the tailgate horizontal can corrode, weaken and fracture. If both break, the tailgate and any supported person or cargo can fall.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall completion. A Chevrolet dealer replaces both tailgate support cables under the no-charge campaign.
symptoms: Corroded or frayed tailgate support cable
Tailgate support cable fractures
Tailgate drops onto the bumper
after.contentUpdateSummary: Replaced an unsupported transmission-failure aggregation with the exact 2002-2004 tailgate-cable recall and removed repair-cost claims.

issues.decision: Replace the secondary-source brake-line investigation summary with the exact 2003 fuel-tank impact-shield recall.

after.title: Frontal Impact Can Puncture the Fuel Tank (Recall 03V019)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 03V019 covers certain 2003 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles. In a sufficiently severe 30-degree left-angle frontal impact, the mid-frame crossmember can tear and form a sharp edge that may puncture the fuel tank, allowing fuel leakage and a possible fire.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall completion. A Chevrolet dealer installs a fuel-tank shield under the no-charge campaign.
symptoms: No reliable warning before the crash-related condition
Fuel leakage after a severe angled frontal impact
affectedSystems: mid-frame crossmember, fuel tank and protective shield
after.contentUpdateSummary: Replaced a secondary brake-line investigation card with the exact 2003 fuel-tank impact-shield recall.

after.title: Heated Washer-Fluid Module Can Ignite (Recall 10V240)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 10V240 covers certain 2007-2009 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles equipped with the heated washer-fluid system. Thermal incidents continued after an earlier fuse remedy; the module can melt or ignite and cause a vehicle fire.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall completion. A Chevrolet dealer permanently disables and removes the heated washer-fluid module and updates the owner manual under the no-charge recall.
symptoms: Melted heated-washer module housing
Electrical odor or smoke
Fire at the heated washer-fluid module
affectedSystems: heated washer-fluid module and electrical circuit

evidence.label: NHTSA Recall 05V163 - Second-Row Center Seat-Belt Routing

after.title: Second-Row Center Lap Belt May Route Too High (Recall 05V163)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 05V163 covers certain 2003-2005 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles. The second-row center seat-belt guide can make it difficult to position the lap belt low and snug on an occupant's hips, increasing abdominal and internal-organ injury risk in a crash.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall completion. A Chevrolet dealer modifies the guide loop and secures the remaining sides with a retainer under the no-charge campaign.
symptoms: Second-row center lap belt rides on the abdomen
Lap belt cannot be positioned low and snug on the hips
affectedSystems: second-row center seat-belt guide and lap-belt routing

after.title: Ignition Lock Can Bind or Snap to Accessory (Recall 14V827)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 14V827 covers certain 2011-2012 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles. The ignition-lock actuator can bind or hold the key in Start, then snap back to Accessory. That can remove engine, steering and braking power and can prevent air-bag deployment in a crash.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall completion. A Chevrolet dealer inspects and replaces the ignition-lock housing as necessary under the no-charge campaign.
symptoms: Key is difficult to turn
Ignition remains in Start
Ignition suddenly snaps to Accessory
Loss of engine, steering or brake power
after.contentUpdateSummary: Replaced an unsupported AFM/oil-consumption aggregation with the exact 2011-2012 ignition-lock recall.

after.title: Hydro-Boost Relief-Valve Seal Can Fracture (Recall 04V045)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 04V045 covers certain 2003-2004 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles built with an out-of-specification hydro-boost housing relief-valve bore. The valve O-ring can fracture, slightly increasing steering effort while braking or parking and, under some conditions, increasing brake-pedal effort.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall completion. A Chevrolet dealer replaces the hydro-boost relief valve under the no-charge campaign.
symptoms: Increased steering effort while braking or parking
Increased brake-pedal effort
affectedSystems: hydro-boost housing relief valve and O-ring seal
after.contentUpdateSummary: Replaced an unsupported HVAC actuator card with the exact 2003-2004 hydro-boost relief-valve recall.

after.title: Transmission Shift-Position Indicator May Not Illuminate (Recall 05V055)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 05V055 covers certain 2005 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles. Under some starting conditions, the instrument-cluster shift-position indicator may not illuminate, so the driver may not know which gear is selected and the vehicle can move in an unintended direction.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall completion. A Chevrolet dealer reprograms the instrument panel cluster under the no-charge campaign.
symptoms: Shift-position indicator does not illuminate after starting
Selected transmission gear is not visible
affectedSystems: instrument panel cluster and shift-position indicator

evidence.label: NHTSA Recall 05V379 - Unwanted Low-Speed ABS Activation

after.title: Corrosion Can Trigger Unwanted Low-Speed ABS Activation (Recall 05V379)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 05V379 includes certain 2002 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles in specified salt-belt jurisdictions. Corrosion at a front wheel-speed sensor mounting surface can weaken the signal and trigger unwanted ABS activation during low-speed braking, increasing stopping distance.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall eligibility and completion because the campaign is geographically limited. The dealer removes the sensor, cleans and protects the mounting surface, reinstalls the sensor and verifies signal voltage.
symptoms: ABS activates during low-speed braking
Brake pedal pulsates near a stop
Stopping distance increases at low speed
affectedSystems: front wheel-speed sensors, hub mounting surfaces and ABS

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 05V379 - Unwanted Low-Speed ABS Activation

after.title: Fuel-Rail Pulse-Damper Retainer Can Fracture (Recall 06V289)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 06V289 covers certain 2004 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles equipped with the 8.1L V8 identified by RPO L8 and VIN code G. The fuel-rail pulse-damper retainer clip can fracture, allowing the damper to loosen and fuel to leak, creating a fire risk near an ignition source.
after.solution: Check the VIN and engine identification for recall completion. A Chevrolet dealer replaces the fuel-rail pulse-damper retainer clip under the no-charge campaign.
symptoms: Fuel odor or leak at the fuel rail
Loose fuel-rail pulse damper
Engine-compartment fire risk
affectedSystems: fuel rail, pulse damper and retainer clip

evidence.label: NHTSA Recall 05V552 - Tire and Loading Information Label

after.title: Tire and Loading Label May List the Wrong Capacity (Recall 05V552)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 05V552 covers certain 2006 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles shipped with a tire-and-loading label that lists an inaccurate vehicle capacity weight. Relying on the incorrect label can contribute to improper loading or tire inflation and increase tire-failure and crash risk.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall completion. GM provides a corrected label and installation instructions, or a dealer installs the corrected label at the owner's option.
symptoms: Original tire-and-loading label lists an inaccurate capacity weight

evidence.label: NHTSA Recall 21V054 - Passenger Frontal Air-Bag Inflator

after.title: Passenger Air-Bag Inflator Can Explode (Recall 21V054)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 21V054 includes certain 2010-2013 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles originally sold or registered in specified Zone B or Zone C jurisdictions. Long-term heat and humidity exposure can degrade the non-desiccated passenger frontal inflator propellant, causing the inflator to explode and propel sharp metal fragments into occupants.
after.solution: Check the VIN because affected model years depend on the vehicle's geographic history. A Chevrolet dealer replaces the front passenger air-bag inflator with an alternate inflator under the no-charge recall.
symptoms: No reliable warning before inflator rupture
Open passenger-air-bag inflator recall for the VIN

evidence.label: NHTSA Recall 09V154 - Fuel-System Control Module Water Intrusion

after.title: Water Can Short the Fuel-System Control Module (Recall 09V154)
after.description: NHTSA Recall 09V154 covers certain 2009 Chevrolet Avalanche vehicles. Separation of the module housing seal can let water enter the fuel-system control module, causing a short or open circuit, warning light and DTCs, hard starting, a no-start condition or an engine stall.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall completion. A Chevrolet dealer installs a new fuel-system control module under the no-charge campaign.
symptoms: Service Engine Soon light
Fuel-system control DTCs
Hard start or no start
Engine stalls
affectedSystems: fuel-system control module and housing seal

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 09V154 - Fuel-System Control Module Water Intrusion
